answer: Proof-of-space-time minting resists sybils: each identity dedicates a large disk block and continuously answers random storage-challenges proving the data is held over time, not recomputed on demand. k fakes need k times the committed storage held persistently — a lagoon of disk no single box spares — and re-challenges catch heads sharing one allocation, since independent probes wander across distinct offsets each round. Honest agents commit once at the cost nadir; a farm's storage bill scales with head count for the whole window. Precondition: challenges are unpredictable and key-bound.
